case_number: Criminal Appeal No.67701-J of 2020 / Criminal Appeal No.67702-J of 2020 / Criminal Revision No.2533 of 2021

facts.location: Barber shop of Zamin Abbas, Market Sarfraz Colony, Jauharabad
facts.summary: The appellants allegedly fired multiple shots at Muhammad Shehzad inside a barber shop, causing fatal injuries. The prosecution relied on two eyewitnesses and alleged motive of prior quarrel.

legal_issues.finding: Complainant had mobile phone but did not inform police immediately; FIR not registered in manner portrayed.
Eyewitnesses were chance witnesses; failed to justify presence at spot; testimony unreliable.
Non-production of barber Zamin Abbas led to adverse presumption under Article 129(g) Qanun-e-Shahadat Order.

legal_issues.issue: Contradiction between medical and ocular evidence
legal_issues.finding: Blackening on wounds inconsistent with alleged firing distance of 6–9 feet; prosecution version doubtful.
PFSA reports silent regarding live cartridges; could not cure defects in prosecution case.
Alleged prior quarrel vague; no specific details; motive not established.
Multiple doubts in prosecution case entitled appellants to acquittal.

appellant: FIR delay; chance witnesses; withholding of material witness; medical contradiction; unreliable forensic report; motive not proved; benefit of doubt.
respondent: FIR registered promptly; eyewitness account consistent; recoveries and PFSA reports support prosecution; motive established.

judgment_summary.Criminal Appeal No.67701-J of 2020: Allowed; conviction and sentence set aside; appellants acquitted
judgment_summary.Criminal Appeal No.67702-J of 2020: Allowed; conviction and sentence set aside; appellant acquitted
judgment_summary.release_of_appellants: Forthwith if not required in any other case

remarks: Due to delay in FIR, unreliable chance witnesses, withholding of material witness, medical contradiction regarding blackening, unreliable forensic reports, and unproven motive, the appellants were acquitted.
